title: Review: Hormonal coordination in humans; Plant hormones biology only; Reproduction
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.5.4-c04 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.3-c15 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.3-c23 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.3-c19 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.5.3-q12, 4.5.3-q25, 4.5.3-q19, 4.5.4-q02, 4.6.1-q02, 4.6.1-q06, 4.5.3-q10, 4.5.3-q16, 4.5.3-q20, 4.5.4-q01, 4.6.1-q01, 4.6.1-q05, 4.5.3-q24. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Auxin
items.clue: A plant hormone whose unequal distribution causes unequal growth rates in plant roots and shoots.

items.label: sweat
items.clue: The liquid lost from the skin, containing water, ions and urea; there is no control over water, ion or urea loss by the skin.

items.label: oestrogen
items.clue: The main female reproductive hormone, produced in the ovary; with progesterone it is involved in maintaining the uterus lining.

items.label: selective reabsorption
items.clue: The taking back into the blood of useful substances such as glucose, some ions and water after the blood has been filtered by the kidneys.

questions.stem: How do the kidneys produce urine and help to maintain the water balance of the body?

options.text: only waste substances are filtered out of the blood
glucose and all useful ions are lost in the urine
urea is reabsorbed and glucose is lost in the urine
the blood is filtered and useful substances reabsorbed

questions.explanation: The kidneys produce urine by filtration of the blood and selective reabsorption of useful substances such as glucose, some ions and water, and excess water, ions and urea are removed in the urine.

questions.stem: Which statement about the main reproductive hormones is correct?

options.text: oestrogen is produced by the pituitary gland
testosterone is produced by the testes
oestrogen is produced by the thyroid gland
testosterone is produced by the pituitary

questions.explanation: Testosterone is the main male reproductive hormone produced by the testes, and it stimulates sperm production.

questions.stem: A woman wants a method of contraception that does not use hormones. Which method and reason are correct?

options.text: a condom, which releases a hormone slowly
a diaphragm, which stops sperm reaching eggs
the pill, which kills sperm before they arrive
an implant, which stops sperm reaching an egg

questions.explanation: Barrier methods such as condoms and diaphragms prevent the sperm reaching an egg, so they control fertility without using hormones.

questions.stem: A seedling is laid on its side in the dark. Which describes the response of its root?

options.text: Auxin gathers on the lower side, which grows more quickly.
Auxin collects on the upper side, which grows slower.
Auxin gathers on the lower side, which grows slower.
Auxin gathers on the upper side, which then grows faster.

questions.explanation: Unequal distribution of auxin gives more auxin on the lower side of the root, where it causes a slower growth rate, so the root bends downwards (gravitropism or geotropism).

questions.stem: Which statement about sexual reproduction in a flowering plant is correct?

options.text: In plants, the gametes made by meiosis are all identical cells.
In plants, pollen and egg cells fuse, mixing genetic information.
In plants, one parent's gametes fuse without a second parent.
In plants, the gametes are made by mitosis in flower organs.

questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction involves the joining (fusion) of male and female gametes, which in flowering plants are pollen and egg cells, and there is mixing of genetic information.

questions.stem: What happens after two gametes join at fertilisation?

options.text: The new cell divides by meiosis, then cells differentiate.
The new cell divides by mitosis and then forms four gametes.
The new cell divides by mitosis and cells differentiate.
The new cell has half the chromosome number of gametes.

questions.explanation: Gametes join at fertilisation to restore the normal number of chromosomes; the new cell divides by mitosis, the number of cells increases, and as the embryo develops cells differentiate.

questions.stem: The body fluids around a person's cells become too dilute. What is the effect on the cells?

options.text: they gain water by osmosis and work as normal
they gain water by osmosis and work less well
they lose water by osmosis and stop working well
they lose water by osmosis and work as normal

questions.explanation: Water moves into the cells by osmosis from the more dilute body fluids, and if body cells gain too much water by osmosis they do not function efficiently.

questions.stem: What is the role of follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) in the menstrual cycle?

options.text: it causes a mature egg to be released
it keeps the lining of the uterus in place
it causes an egg to mature in the ovary
it is released from the ovary at puberty

questions.explanation: Follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) causes maturation of an egg in the ovary.

questions.stem: How do oral contraceptives that contain hormones prevent pregnancy?

options.text: they inhibit FSH production so no eggs mature
they kill or disable sperm before fertilisation
they stop an embryo implanting in the uterus
they form a barrier that stops sperm reaching eggs

questions.explanation: Oral contraceptives contain hormones to inhibit FSH production so that no eggs mature.

questions.stem: A young shoot is lit from one side only and bends towards the light. Which explains this?

options.text: Auxin gathers on the lit side, which grows faster.
Auxin gathers on the shaded side, which grows less.
Auxin gathers on the shaded side, which grows faster.
Auxin gathers on the lit side, which then grows slower.

questions.explanation: Unequal distribution of auxin gives more auxin on the shaded side of the shoot, which produces a faster growth rate on that side, so the shoot bends towards the light (phototropism).

questions.stem: Which statement describes the cells formed by meiosis?

options.text: They are all genetically identical to each other.
They are all genetically different from each other.
There are two of them formed from the parent cell.
They each contain the full number of chromosomes.

questions.explanation: Meiosis leads to non-identical cells being formed: all gametes are genetically different from each other.

questions.stem: A body cell of a species contains 20 chromosomes. What happens to chromosome number during reproduction?

options.text: Meiosis gives gametes with 20; fertilisation reduces to 10.
Meiosis gives gametes with 10; fertilisation restores 20.
Meiosis gives two gametes with 10; fertilisation gives 20.
Meiosis gives gametes with 20; fertilisation restores 40.

questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the number of chromosomes in gametes, so each gamete has a single set of 10, and fertilisation restores the full number of 20.

questions.stem: The concentration of thyroxine in the blood of a person rises above the normal level. What happens next?

options.text: more thyroxine is released and the level rises
the metabolic rate falls and the level stays high
the metabolic rate falls and more thyroxine forms
thyroxine release is inhibited and the level falls

questions.explanation: Thyroxine levels are controlled by negative feedback, so a level above normal inhibits the release of thyroxine until the level returns to normal.
